note: A small synthetic seed for a fresh install: one three-row supersession chain, one cross-tier contested pair, a dead end with its falsifier, a target, a mission whose second gate reads null, and the same predicate held at two scopes to show nearest-scope-wins.

assertions.subject: api
assertions.claim: Every Acme service may burn up to 1.0 percent of requests in a 30-day window before the error budget freezes releases.

evidence.source: reliability policy v3, org-wide, ratified at the 2026-01-15 platform review

assertions.subject: api
assertions.claim: Checkout runs on a tighter error budget than the rest of Acme: 0.5 percent per 30-day window, because a failed checkout is a lost order rather than a retried page view.

evidence.source: checkout reliability addendum, agreed at the 2026-03-02 checkout review; tightens the org-wide 1.0 percent for this project only

assertions.subject: api
assertions.claim: Checkout API p99 latency is 820 ms under the standard load profile.

evidence.protocol: 30 minutes at 400 requests/second, p99 over produced responses, one region

assertions.subject: api
assertions.claim: Checkout API p99 latency is 410 ms after the payment-provider calls were moved off the request path.

evidence.protocol: 30 minutes at 400 requests/second, p99 over produced responses, one region

assertions.subject: api
assertions.claim: Checkout API p99 latency is 180 ms after the cart-total cache landed. This is the live figure; 410 ms and 820 ms are its history.

evidence.protocol: 30 minutes at 400 requests/second, p99 over produced responses, one region

assertions.subject: api
assertions.claim: Target: checkout API p99 latency at or below 150 ms, closable only by a measured figure.

evidence.source: checkout quarterly objective, set at the 2026-07-06 planning session

assertions.subject: checkout

object.unit: percent of sessions completing an order

assertions.claim: Checkout conversion is 2.4 percent of sessions, measured over the July analytics window with bot traffic excluded.

evidence.protocol: sessions reaching /checkout divided by completed orders, July 2026, bot traffic excluded

assertions.subject: checkout

object.unit: percent of sessions completing an order

assertions.claim: Conversion is 3.1 percent, not 2.4: the warehouse export drops guest sessions that complete on a second device, so the instrument undercounts.

evidence.source: product review notes 2026-07-30, reconciling the warehouse export against payment-processor settlements
evidence.protocol: settled orders from the payment processor over the same July window, divided by warehouse session count

assertions.subject: checkout

object.unit: percent of settled orders refunded within 30 days

assertions.claim: Refund rate is about 1.2 percent of settled orders within 30 days, read off the finance dashboard by hand. No instrumented figure exists yet.

evidence.source: finance dashboard, read during the 2026-07-30 product review; no query or export was captured

assertions.subject: payment:wallet-redirect

object.arm: wallet redirect vs inline card form

assertions.claim: Dead end: redirecting to the wallet provider cost 18 percent of completed checkouts against the inline card form.

evidence.source: A/B experiment exp-2026-06-wallet-redirect, 41,882 sessions per arm
evidence.protocol: two-arm split at 50/50 for 14 days, primary metric completed checkouts per session

assertions.why: The redirect drops the customer on the wallet provider's own domain, and 18 percent of them never come back. The loss is concentrated in the first-time-buyer segment, which is the segment the redirect was supposed to help.
assertions.reopen_if: the wallet provider ships an inline SDK that keeps the customer on acme.com, or a re-run shows first-time-buyer completion within 2 percent of the inline card form.

missions.statement: Get checkout p99 under 150 ms without letting refunds drift above 1.5 percent.

gates.subject: api
gates.note: The live figure is 180 ms; 410 ms and 820 ms are superseded and must never be read back as current.

gates.subject: checkout
gates.note: A human read 1.2 percent off a dashboard, but testimony cannot satisfy a gate that demands a measurement - so this gate reads null, not true. Instrument the refund query to close it.
